guidelineReading.description: A measured value beside the guideline it is read against. A ratio above 1 is past the guideline. Guidelines order and annotate results; they do not hide them.

ratio.description: value divided by guideline, two decimals.

includeResolution.description: Present only when the tree has C or C++ files: where the include directories came from and how many quoted includes found no file. A warning is printed on stderr and a notice added to a table when the share is above the plugin's unresolvedIncludePercent guideline. Nothing is hidden.

compileCommands.description: The compile_commands.json files the include directories came from, or null when none was read. tracked is false for a file read from disk that git does not track.

inferredRoots.description: Directories inferred from where the included files are. Inferred only with neither a compile_commands.json nor includeRoots.

includes.description: Includes that name a file of the repository or look for one: every quoted include, and every angle include that resolved.

unresolved.description: Quoted includes that found no file.

envelope.description: Fields every document has. A command schema adds its own `command` and `results` and closes the document with unevaluatedProperties.

omittedByBuiltinExcludes.description: Present only when a built-in exclude omitted files: the number of files each built-in entry omitted (.claude/**, .cache/**, .code-health/**, or a directory below the repository root that is its own git checkout). Entries that omitted nothing are not listed.

dropped.description: Present only when files were left out because of what they are: the number of distinct files left out as generated (a linguist-generated attribute, a minified file, a path with a segment named generated, a match of the config's generatedPatterns, or a generated-code header), as vendored (a linguist-vendored attribute or a vendor directory), and as non-code (no language adapter or lexical profile claims them, for a command that ranks only code), and as tests (a command that lists production code first, left out unless `--include-tests` is given). Kinds that left out nothing are not listed.

meta.description: Wall-clock facts. Absent from reports and ignored by golden comparisons.
